task_3.title: Add load_datatree() for eager loading of DataTree from disk
task_3.description: Introduces a new top-level function xarray.load_datatree() that opens a DataTree from a file or file-like object, eagerly loads all contents into memory, and closes the underlying file handle before returning. This mirrors the existing relationship between load_dataset() and open_dataset(), giving users a convenient one-call pattern for DataTree objects when lazy loading is not needed. Additionally, internal fixes ensure that DataTree variable protection correctly operates on each node's dataset, and a new delayed_close_after_writes helper is added for dask-based store finalization.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can eagerly load a DataTree entirely into memory from a file or file-like object in a single call, analogous to how load_dataset() works for Dataset. Previously, users had to manually call open_datatree(), invoke .load(), and close the file handle themselves. The new load_datatree() function should handle all three steps automatically and be accessible as a top-level xarray API.

expectation.grounded: xarray.load_datatree(filename_or_obj, **kwargs) must return a fully in-memory DataTree with all file handles closed. It must accept the same parameters as open_datatree() and forward them. If the caller passes a 'cache' keyword argument, load_datatree must raise a TypeError. The function must be exported from the xarray top-level namespace and included in __all__. Internally, _protect_datatree_variables_inplace must correctly pass each node's dataset (not the node itself) when protecting variables.
expectation.conceptual: A new top-level convenience function must allow users to open, fully load, and close a DataTree in one call. The function mirrors the load_dataset/open_dataset pattern. The returned DataTree must be entirely in memory with no lingering file handles. Passing the 'cache' parameter must be rejected with a clear error since it has no effect in this eager-load context.

constraints.grounded: load_datatree must not leave file handles open after returning. It must raise TypeError when 'cache' is supplied in kwargs. All existing open_datatree parameters must be accepted and forwarded without modification. The function must appear in xarray.__all__ and be importable as xarray.load_datatree. The existing load_dataset and load_dataarray functions must remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: The new function must not introduce resource leaks. It must reject inapplicable parameters with appropriate errors rather than silently ignoring them. Existing dataset and dataarray loading APIs must continue to work identically. The DataTree returned must behave identically to one obtained by manually calling open_datatree followed by .load().

behavior: Calling xarray.load_datatree(path) opens the file, eagerly loads the full DataTree into memory, closes the file handle, and returns the DataTree.
All keyword arguments accepted by open_datatree are forwarded transparently to open_datatree.
Passing cache as a keyword argument raises TypeError with a message indicating cache has no effect.
The returned DataTree contains no lazy/deferred arrays — all data is loaded into memory.
After load_datatree returns, the underlying file or store is closed and no file handles remain open.
load_datatree is importable directly from the xarray top-level package.
Internal DataTree variable protection now correctly operates on each node's dataset rather than the node object itself.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls xarray.load_datatree(path_to_file), it should return a DataTree with all data loaded into memory and no open file handles.
When a user calls xarray.load_datatree(path, cache=True), it should raise a TypeError.
When a user imports load_datatree from xarray (i.e., from xarray import load_datatree), the import should succeed.
When a user inspects xarray.__all__, 'load_datatree' should be present.
Given a file containing a DataTree, when load_datatree is called, the result should be identical to calling open_datatree followed by .load() on the returned tree.
When load_datatree returns, attempting to access any variable in any node of the returned DataTree should not trigger any file I/O.
Existing calls to load_dataset and load_dataarray should continue to behave identically after this change.

task_2.title: Add convenience methods to Coordinates (rename, drop, merge operator)
task_2.description: The Coordinates class in xarray now exposes convenience methods for renaming dimensions and variables, dropping variables and dimensions, and merging two Coordinates objects using the | operator. Previously, users had to convert Coordinates to a Dataset, perform these operations, and extract .coords back. These methods provide a direct, ergonomic API on Coordinates itself, preparing for a future refactor where Coordinates no longer wraps a Dataset internally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the xarray Coordinates class provides direct convenience methods for common coordinate manipulation tasks: renaming dimensions (rename_dims), renaming variables (rename_vars), dropping variables (drop_vars), dropping dimensions (drop_dims), and merging two Coordinates objects via the | (or) operator. Users should not need to round-trip through a Dataset to perform these operations.

expectation.grounded: Coordinates.rename_dims(dims_dict, **dims) returns a new Coordinates with renamed dimensions. Coordinates.rename_vars(name_dict, **names) returns a new Coordinates with renamed variables. Coordinates.drop_vars(names, errors='raise'|'ignore') returns a new Coordinates with the specified variables (and their dependent indexes) removed; when errors='raise', a ValueError is raised for names not present. Coordinates.drop_dims(drop_dims, errors='raise'|'ignore') returns a new Coordinates without the specified dimensions or any coordinates containing those dimensions; when errors='raise', a ValueError is raised for dimensions not present. The | operator (Coordinates.__or__) accepts another Coordinates or dict-like mapping and returns a merged Coordinates following the same conflict-resolution rules as Coordinates.merge: conflicting index coordinates raise an exception, a conflicting index vs non-index coordinate drops the non-index coordinate, and two conflicting non-index coordinates are both dropped.
expectation.conceptual: The Coordinates object supports direct renaming of dimensions and variables, dropping of variables and dimensions with configurable error handling, and merging of two coordinate sets using the pipe operator. All operations return new Coordinates objects without mutating the original. The merge operator follows established xarray conflict-resolution semantics for index and non-index coordinates.

constraints.grounded: All new methods must return Coordinates (or Self) objects, not Dataset objects. The drop_vars and drop_dims methods must support an errors parameter with 'raise' (default) and 'ignore' options matching existing Dataset behavior. The drop_vars names parameter must accept a string, an iterable of hashables, or a callable that receives the object and returns names. The | operator must be consistent with Coordinates.merge semantics. Existing Coordinates behavior (e.g., __setitem__, merge, assign, update) must not be altered.
constraints.conceptual: New convenience methods must preserve the existing semantics of the equivalent Dataset operations. Error handling modes must be consistent with the rest of the xarray API. The merge operator must follow the same conflict-resolution rules as the existing merge method. No existing Coordinates functionality should regress.

behavior: Calling Coordinates.rename_dims with a dimension mapping returns a new Coordinates object where the specified dimensions are renamed, without affecting variable names.
Calling Coordinates.rename_vars with a variable name mapping returns a new Coordinates object where the specified coordinate variable names are renamed.

Calling Coordinates.drop_vars with variable names removes those variables and any indexes that depend on them; raises ValueError by default if a name is not found, or silently ignores missing names when errors='ignore'.
Calling Coordinates.drop_vars with a callable passes the Coordinates object to the callable and uses the returned names for dropping.

Calling Coordinates.drop_dims with dimension names removes those dimensions and all coordinates associated with them; raises ValueError by default if a dimension is not found, or silently ignores missing dimensions when errors='ignore'.
Using coords1 | coords2 returns a new merged Coordinates object equivalent to coords1.merge(coords2).coords.

When merging via |, conflicting index coordinates raise an exception, a conflict between an index and non-index coordinate drops the non-index, and two conflicting non-index coordinates are both dropped.
acceptance_criteria: When a Coordinates object has dimensions 'x' and 'y', calling rename_dims({'x': 'a'}) should return a new Coordinates with dimension 'a' in place of 'x', while 'y' remains unchanged.
When a Coordinates object has variables 'lon' and 'lat', calling rename_vars({'lon': 'longitude'}) should return a new Coordinates with 'longitude' replacing 'lon'.
When calling drop_vars('x') on a Coordinates object containing variable 'x', the returned Coordinates should not contain 'x' or any index that depended on 'x'.
When calling drop_vars('nonexistent') with errors='raise' (default), a ValueError should be raised.
When calling drop_vars('nonexistent', errors='ignore'), no error should be raised and the Coordinates should be returned unchanged.
When calling drop_vars with a callable that returns ['x'], the variable 'x' should be dropped from the result.
When calling drop_dims('x') on a Coordinates object with dimension 'x', all coordinates along that dimension should be removed from the result.
When calling drop_dims('nonexistent') with errors='raise', a ValueError should be raised.
When calling drop_dims('nonexistent', errors='ignore'), no error should be raised.
When using coords1 | coords2 where both have compatible index coordinates, the result should contain the merged set of all coordinates.
When using coords1 | coords2 where index coordinates conflict, an exception should be raised.
When using coords1 | coords2 where a non-index coordinate conflicts with an index coordinate, the non-index coordinate should be dropped.
When using coords1 | coords2 where two non-index coordinates conflict, both should be dropped from the result.
All new methods should return Coordinates objects, not Dataset objects.
The original Coordinates object should remain unmodified after any of these operations.

task_5.title: Fix open_dataset zarr backend inference for paths with trailing slash
task_5.description: Previously, calling open_dataset with a path ending in a trailing slash (e.g., 'data.zarr/') failed to automatically infer the zarr backend, because the extension extraction logic returned an empty string for such paths. This fix ensures that trailing slashes are stripped before checking the file extension, so paths like 'data.zarr/' are correctly recognized as zarr stores without requiring the user to explicitly specify engine='zarr'.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that open_dataset correctly auto-detects the zarr backend when the file path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., 'data.zarr/'). Previously, a trailing slash caused the backend inference to fail, requiring users to explicitly pass engine='zarr' even though the path clearly indicated a zarr store. This commonly occurs when paths are constructed via shell autocomplete or programmatic directory listing.

expectation.grounded: ZarrBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open should return True for string or os.PathLike inputs whose path, after stripping any trailing slash, has a '.zarr' extension. open_dataset should automatically select the zarr backend for paths such as 'data.zarr/' without requiring the user to specify the engine parameter explicitly.
expectation.conceptual: When a user calls open_dataset with a path to a zarr store that includes a trailing slash, the library should automatically detect and use the zarr backend, behaving identically to when the path has no trailing slash.

constraints.grounded: Paths without a trailing slash (e.g., 'data.zarr') must continue to be correctly inferred as zarr. Non-zarr paths must not be misidentified as zarr regardless of trailing slashes. guess_can_open must still return False for non-string, non-PathLike inputs.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter behavior for paths that already worked correctly. Only paths with a trailing slash that were previously unrecognized should now be handled. No other backend inference logic should be affected.

behavior: open_dataset('data.zarr/') now automatically selects the zarr backend, whereas previously it failed to infer the backend and raised an error or fell back to an incorrect engine.
ZarrBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open returns True for paths like 'data.zarr/' (with trailing slash), matching the existing behavior for 'data.zarr' (without trailing slash).
Trailing slashes are normalized before extension extraction, so the extension check operates on the canonical form of the path.
Non-string, non-PathLike inputs continue to return False from guess_can_open.
acceptance_criteria: When open_dataset is called with a path 'data.zarr/' (trailing slash), it should automatically use the zarr backend without the user specifying engine='zarr'.
When open_dataset is called with a path 'data.zarr' (no trailing slash), it should continue to automatically use the zarr backend as before.
When ZarrBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open is called with 'data.zarr/', it should return True.
When ZarrBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open is called with 'data.zarr', it should return True.
When ZarrBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open is called with a non-zarr path such as 'data.nc/', it should return False.
When ZarrBackendEntrypoint.guess_can_open is called with a non-string, non-PathLike object, it should return False.

task_1.title: Support rechunking by SeasonResampler for seasonal data analysis
task_1.description: Previously, Dataset.chunk() only accepted TimeResampler objects for datetime-like dimensions, causing obscure errors when users attempted to use SeasonResampler for seasonal chunking. This change generalizes the chunking mechanism to work with any Resampler subclass by introducing a compute_chunks method on the Resampler base class, with concrete implementations in both TimeResampler and SeasonResampler. The SeasonResampler implementation forces drop_incomplete=False during chunking to prevent silent data loss. Error messages are also improved with clearer context, and a validation ensures the season specification covers all 12 months when rechunking.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.chunk() accepts SeasonResampler (and any Resampler subclass) for datetime-like dimensions, not only TimeResampler. Ensure that passing a SeasonResampler to Dataset.chunk() computes correct seasonal chunk boundaries without silently dropping data. Ensure that improved error messages are raised when rechunking is attempted on virtual variables or non-1D variables. Ensure that SeasonResampler rechunking validates that the provided seasons cover all 12 months.

expectation.grounded: Dataset.chunk() accepts any Resampler subclass (including SeasonResampler and TimeResampler) via the chunks parameter for datetime-like dimensions. The Resampler base class exposes a compute_chunks(variable, dim) method that returns a tuple of chunk sizes; it raises NotImplementedError if not overridden. TimeResampler.compute_chunks raises ValueError if the variable does not contain datetime-like objects. SeasonResampler.compute_chunks raises ValueError if the variable is not datetime-like or if the seasons do not cover all 12 months. During chunking, SeasonResampler internally sets drop_incomplete=False to prevent data loss. The type alias T_ChunkDimFreq accepts Resampler instead of only TimeResampler. A ValueError is raised for virtual variables (including the variable name in the message) and for variables that are not 1D. A safety check raises ValueError if the computed chunks do not sum to the variable size.
expectation.conceptual: Users can pass any supported Resampler object (such as SeasonResampler or TimeResampler) to Dataset.chunk() on datetime dimensions to control how data is split into chunks along that dimension. The chunking operation computes chunk boundaries based on the resampler's grouping strategy and returns correctly sized chunks without silently dropping any data. Clear, descriptive errors are raised when the input variable is incompatible with resampler-based chunking or when the seasonal specification is incomplete.

constraints.grounded: Existing TimeResampler chunking behavior must remain unchanged — TimeResampler.compute_chunks must produce identical chunk tuples as the previous inline implementation. SeasonResampler must override drop_incomplete to False internally during compute_chunks without mutating the user-facing instance. SeasonResampler.compute_chunks must reject season specifications that do not cover all 12 months. The sum of the returned chunk tuple must equal the variable's dimension size. Resampler.compute_chunks must raise NotImplementedError for subclasses that do not implement it. The isinstance check in Dataset.chunk() must use the Resampler base class, not TimeResampler.
constraints.conceptual: Backward compatibility with existing TimeResampler-based chunking must be preserved. No data may be silently dropped during seasonal rechunking. Only resamplers that fully cover the calendar (all 12 months) are permitted for rechunking. The chunking output must always be consistent with the actual variable size. Custom Resampler subclasses that do not implement chunk computation must fail explicitly.

behavior: Dataset.chunk() now dispatches to Resampler.compute_chunks() for any Resampler subclass, not just TimeResampler
SeasonResampler can be passed to Dataset.chunk() (e.g., ds.chunk(time=SeasonResampler(['DJF', 'MAM', 'JJA', 'SON']))) and produces correct seasonal chunk boundaries
SeasonResampler.compute_chunks internally creates a copy with drop_incomplete=False, preventing silent data loss during chunking
SeasonResampler.compute_chunks raises ValueError if the provided seasons do not cover all 12 months
TimeResampler.compute_chunks raises ValueError when applied to a non-datetime variable
Dataset.chunk() raises ValueError with the variable name when a Resampler is used on a virtual variable
Dataset.chunk() raises ValueError when a Resampler is used on a variable with more than 1 dimension
A safety check raises ValueError if the computed chunk sizes do not sum to the variable's total size
SeasonResampler and SeasonGrouper are now exported in the groupers module __all__ list
The T_ChunkDimFreq type alias accepts any Resampler, not just TimeResampler
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls Dataset.chunk(time=SeasonResampler(['DJF', 'MAM', 'JJA', 'SON'])) on a dataset with a datetime time dimension, it should return a chunked dataset with chunk boundaries aligned to seasonal periods
When a user calls Dataset.chunk(time=TimeResampler(freq='YE')) on a dataset with a datetime time dimension, it should produce the same results as before this change
When SeasonResampler is used for chunking, the drop_incomplete setting on the user's instance should not affect the chunking result — no data should be silently dropped
When SeasonResampler.compute_chunks is called with seasons that do not cover all 12 months, it should raise a ValueError indicating incomplete month coverage
When a Resampler is passed for a virtual variable (one not in the dataset's internal variables), it should raise a ValueError mentioning the variable name
When a Resampler is passed for a multi-dimensional variable, it should raise a ValueError stating that only 1D variables are supported
When a Resampler subclass does not implement compute_chunks, calling it should raise NotImplementedError
When the computed chunks do not sum to the variable's dimension size, a ValueError should be raised indicating a logic bug and requesting the user open an issue

task_4.title: Support compute=False for DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr()
task_4.description: DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() now support the compute=False parameter, enabling deferred (lazy) writing via dask.delayed. Previously, these methods always computed immediately and the documentation noted that compute=False was not supported. The implementation was refactored so that each method opens a single root writable store and uses a new get_child_store() API to obtain sub-group stores for each tree node, writes all nodes through a shared ArrayWriter, and returns a dask.delayed.Delayed object when compute=False. Proper overloaded type signatures were added so that static type checkers can distinguish the return type based on the compute argument. Store creation logic was extracted into reusable get_writable_netcdf_store() and get_writable_zarr_store() factory functions. Resource management was also improved: stores are synced (but not closed) when compute=False, and a delayed_close_after_writes() helper ensures the store is closed only after all deferred writes complete.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() support the compute=False parameter, returning a dask.delayed.Delayed object that allows users to defer the actual data writing to a later point. Previously, passing compute=False to these methods had no effect or was explicitly unsupported, forcing users to always write synchronously even when working with chunked (dask-backed) data in a DataTree.

expectation.grounded: When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with a file path and compute=False, it must return a dask.delayed.Delayed object instead of None. When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with compute=False, it must return a dask.delayed.Delayed object instead of a ZarrStore. Calling .compute() on the returned Delayed must complete all pending array writes and close the underlying store. When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with compute=False and no file path (in-memory target), it must raise NotImplementedError. The overloaded type signatures on DataTree.to_netcdf() must reflect: compute=False returns Delayed, filepath=None returns memoryview, and the default (compute=True with filepath) returns None. The overloaded type signatures on DataTree.to_zarr() must reflect: compute=False returns Delayed, and compute=True returns ZarrStore. The underlying backend stores (NetCDF4DataStore, H5NetCDFStore, ZarrStore) must each implement a get_child_store() method that returns a store for a child group within the same file/archive. A sync() method must be available on AbstractWritableDataStore, and stores must call sync() instead of close() when compute=False so that metadata is flushed but the store remains open for deferred writes. The factory functions get_writable_netcdf_store() and get_writable_zarr_store() must be usable to create writable stores independently of the Dataset-level to_netcdf()/to_zarr() codepaths.
expectation.conceptual: When a user writes a DataTree to netCDF or Zarr with deferred computation enabled, the method should return a lazy handle (a Delayed object) that, when computed, completes all data writes and finalizes the file. The user should be able to integrate this into larger dask task graphs. When deferred computation is not applicable (e.g., writing to an in-memory buffer for netCDF), the method should raise a clear error. With the default synchronous mode, behavior should remain unchanged: netCDF writes return None (or memoryview for in-memory), and Zarr writes return the store object. All tree nodes should be written through a single root store using a hierarchical child-store mechanism, rather than opening and closing separate stores per node.

constraints.grounded: Existing behavior of DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() with compute=True (the default) must remain unchanged. DataTree.to_netcdf() with filepath=None must still return a memoryview. DataTree.to_zarr() with compute=True must still return a ZarrStore. The store must not be closed prematurely when compute=False; it must remain open until the Delayed is computed. Consolidated metadata handling for Zarr must be delegated to the store's consolidate_on_close mechanism rather than calling zarr.consolidate_metadata() directly after iteration. The get_child_store() method must propagate the parent store's mode, lock, autoclose, and other configuration to child stores. AbstractDataStore.get_child_store() and AbstractWritableDataStore.sync() must exist as base interface methods.
constraints.conceptual: Default synchronous write behavior must not regress. File resources must be managed correctly in both deferred and immediate modes — no premature closes that would corrupt deferred writes, and no resource leaks that would leave files locked. The hierarchical store mechanism must correctly handle nested groups in the DataTree. Metadata consolidation for Zarr must still occur at the appropriate time.

behavior: DataTree.to_netcdf(filepath, compute=False) returns a dask.delayed.Delayed; computing it writes all array data and closes the store.
DataTree.to_zarr(store, compute=False) returns a dask.delayed.Delayed; computing it writes all array data and closes the store.
DataTree.to_netcdf(filepath=None, compute=False) raises NotImplementedError.
DataTree.to_netcdf(filepath, compute=True) returns None as before.
DataTree.to_netcdf(filepath=None, compute=True) returns memoryview as before.
DataTree.to_zarr(store, compute=True) returns ZarrStore as before.
All tree nodes are written through a single root store using get_child_store() for sub-groups, rather than opening separate stores per node.
When compute=False, the store is synced (metadata flushed) but not closed; closure is deferred via delayed_close_after_writes().
When compute=True, the store is closed immediately after writing in a finally block.
NetCDF4DataStore, H5NetCDFStore, and ZarrStore each implement get_child_store() returning a child-group store of the same type.
Type overloads on DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() enable static type checkers to infer the correct return type based on the compute parameter.
acceptance_criteria: When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with a file path and compute=False on a DataTree containing dask-backed variables, it should return a dask.delayed.Delayed object without writing array data to disk.
When the returned Delayed from DataTree.to_netcdf(compute=False) is computed, the resulting netCDF file should contain all groups and variables from the DataTree.
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with compute=False on a DataTree containing dask-backed variables, it should return a dask.delayed.Delayed object without writing array data to the store.
When the returned Delayed from DataTree.to_zarr(compute=False) is computed, the resulting Zarr store should contain all groups and variables from the DataTree.
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with no file path and compute=False, it should raise NotImplementedError.
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with compute=True (the default), it should write synchronously and return None, matching prior behavior.
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with no file path and compute=True, it should return a memoryview, matching prior behavior.
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with compute=True (the default), it should write synchronously and return a ZarrStore, matching prior behavior.
Given a DataTree with multiple nested groups, when written with compute=False to netCDF or Zarr, all groups and their variables should be present in the output after computing the Delayed.
The Delayed returned by compute=False should, when computed, properly close the underlying file/store so that no resource leaks occur.
Static type checkers should infer Delayed as the return type when compute=False is passed as a literal, and the appropriate synchronous return type when compute=True.

task_6.title: Reclassify Day offset as non-Tick-like for CFTime resampling
task_6.description: Following pandas 3.0, the Day cftime offset is no longer classified as a Tick-like frequency in xarray. This changes the resampling behavior for CFTimeIndex objects at daily frequency: the 'offset' and 'origin' parameters no longer take effect and RuntimeWarnings are emitted when non-default values are provided. The delta_to_tick utility no longer produces Day instances, instead converting whole-day timedeltas into Hour equivalents. CFTimeIndex rounding methods now handle Day as a special case, treating it as a fixed 24-hour timedelta rather than delegating to Tick machinery.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the Day cftime offset is treated as a non-Tick-like frequency, consistent with pandas 3.0 semantics. Ensure that when resampling CFTimeIndex data at daily frequency, the 'offset' parameter (when not None) and the 'origin' parameter (when not 'start_day') are silently ignored but produce RuntimeWarning diagnostics. Ensure that timedelta-to-offset conversion no longer yields Day instances, producing Hour-based equivalents instead. Ensure that CFTimeIndex rounding operations still work correctly with Day frequency by treating it as a 24-hour fixed duration.

expectation.grounded: The Day class must inherit from BaseCFTimeOffset instead of Tick and must be removed from the CFTIME_TICKS collection, which should contain only Hour, Minute, and Second. Day must implement onOffset returning True for all dates and __apply__ that returns a timedelta-based result or combines with other Day instances. CFTimeGrouper must emit a RuntimeWarning via emit_user_level_warning when a non-Tick-like freq (including Day) is used with a non-None offset or a non-'start_day' origin. The delta_to_tick function must convert whole-day timedeltas to Hour objects (e.g., 1 day becomes Hour(n=24)). CFTimeIndex._round_via_method must handle Day by computing offset_as_timedelta as timedelta(days=offset.n) rather than calling as_timedelta.
expectation.conceptual: The Day offset must behave as a calendar-day frequency, not a sub-daily tick. Resampling at daily frequency should not be influenced by offset or origin parameters; when users supply non-default values for these parameters with a daily or coarser frequency, the library should warn them that those arguments have no effect. Timedelta-to-offset conversion should always produce tick-level offsets (hours, minutes, seconds). Rounding operations on CFTimeIndex should continue to support Day frequency by internally treating it as a 24-hour duration.

constraints.grounded: Day must no longer be a subclass of Tick or appear in CFTIME_TICKS. Day must not expose an as_timedelta method inherited from Tick. Existing Hour, Minute, and Second offsets must remain Tick subclasses and continue to work unchanged. The warning must be a RuntimeWarning emitted through emit_user_level_warning. CFTimeIndex.shift with fractional Day multiples should use hour-based frequency notation (e.g., '24h') rather than 'D'. The round/floor/ceil methods must not raise when given a Day frequency.
constraints.conceptual: Sub-daily tick offsets (hours, minutes, seconds) must be unaffected by this change. Only the Day offset changes its classification. Warnings must be user-visible runtime warnings, not errors. Rounding and shifting operations with Day frequency must continue to produce correct results despite the reclassification. No existing valid resampling workflows using tick-level frequencies should be broken.

behavior: Day inherits from BaseCFTimeOffset instead of Tick, making it a non-Tick-like offset
CFTIME_TICKS is reduced to (Hour, Minute, Second), excluding Day
Day.__apply__ combines with other Day instances via addition of n values, and applies to dates via timedelta(days=n)
Day.onOffset always returns True for any date
CFTimeGrouper emits a RuntimeWarning when offset is not None and freq is not in CFTIME_TICKS
CFTimeGrouper emits a RuntimeWarning when origin is not 'start_day' and freq is not in CFTIME_TICKS
delta_to_tick converts whole-day timedeltas to Hour objects instead of Day objects
CFTimeIndex._round_via_method handles Day specially by computing timedelta(days=offset.n) instead of calling as_timedelta
CFTimeIndex.shift documentation reflects using '24h' notation instead of 'D' for fractional-day shifts
acceptance_criteria: When resampling a CFTimeIndex-indexed object with freq='D' and a non-None offset, a RuntimeWarning is emitted indicating the offset keyword has no effect
When resampling a CFTimeIndex-indexed object with freq='D' and origin set to something other than 'start_day', a RuntimeWarning is emitted indicating the origin keyword has no effect
When resampling with freq='D' and default offset (None) and default origin ('start_day'), no warning is emitted
When resampling with a Tick-like frequency (e.g., 'h', 'min', 's') and non-default offset or origin, no warning is emitted and both parameters take effect as before
When converting a timedelta of exactly N days to a CFTime offset via delta_to_tick, the result is an Hour instance with n=N*24, not a Day instance
When calling round, floor, or ceil on a CFTimeIndex with freq='D', the operation succeeds and returns correctly rounded dates
Day instances are not recognized as instances of Tick
Day.onOffset returns True for any cftime date
When applying a Day offset to a cftime date, the result is the date plus the corresponding number of calendar days

task_8.title: to_netcdf() returns memoryview instead of bytes and uses consistent default engine
task_8.description: The return value of Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() called without a path is now always a memoryview object instead of bytes. This eliminates an unnecessary memory copy and unifies behavior across the scipy and h5netcdf engines. Additionally, the default engine selection for to_netcdf is now consistent with open_dataset and open_datatree, preferring netCDF4 over h5netcdf over scipy, rather than hardcoding scipy for in-memory or file-like writes. The previously emitted FutureWarning about this upcoming change has been removed. A minor bug fix ensures that calling to_netcdf with compute=False and path=None raises NotImplementedError referencing memoryview rather than bytes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() return a memoryview (not bytes) when called without a path argument. Ensure that the default engine for in-memory and file-like-object serialization is selected using the same preference order as open_dataset (netCDF4 > h5netcdf > scipy) instead of always defaulting to scipy. Ensure the previously emitted FutureWarning about the bytes-to-memoryview transition is removed. Ensure that calling to_netcdf with compute=False and no path raises NotImplementedError with a message referencing memoryview.

expectation.grounded: When Dataset.to_netcdf() or DataArray.to_netcdf() is called with path=None, the return type annotation and runtime return value must be memoryview, not bytes or bytes | memoryview. The overload signatures for the no-path case must declare the return type as memoryview. The BytesIOProxy class must no longer be generic over bytes and memoryview; its retrieval method must be named getbuffer and must return memoryview. The ScipyDataStore must no longer emit a FutureWarning when writing to a BytesIOProxy. The default engine for writing to file-like objects or returning in-memory data must be resolved via get_default_netcdf_write_engine, which follows the same engine preference logic as open_dataset. When compute=False and path is None, a NotImplementedError must be raised.
expectation.conceptual: When serializing a dataset or data array to netCDF in memory (no file path provided), the result must be a memoryview object, avoiding an extra memory copy. The default engine for in-memory serialization must follow the same preference order used when opening datasets. No deprecation or future warnings related to the return type should be emitted. Attempting lazy (deferred) in-memory serialization must raise a clear not-implemented error.

constraints.grounded: Existing code that passes the return value of to_netcdf() to APIs expecting bytes must wrap it with bytes(). The union type bytes | memoryview must not appear in the return type of to_netcdf overloads for the no-path case. The BytesIOProxy must not retain the deprecated getvalue_or_getbuffer method or the BytesOrMemory TypeVar. The scipy engine must assign getbuffer (not getvalue) on the BytesIOProxy source. The NotImplementedError for compute=False must only be raised when path_or_file is None, not for file-like objects.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not break serialization to file paths or file-like objects. Callers that need bytes must be able to convert from memoryview trivially. Engine selection for writing must remain overridable by the user. Deferred computation for file-based writes must continue to work.

behavior: Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataArray.to_netcdf() with path=None return memoryview instead of bytes
The default engine for in-memory or file-like-object writes is now resolved via get_default_netcdf_write_engine with preference order netCDF4 > h5netcdf > scipy, matching open_dataset behavior
The FutureWarning previously emitted by ScipyDataStore when writing to BytesIOProxy is removed
BytesIOProxy is no longer generic; it always produces memoryview via a getbuffer() method
Calling to_netcdf with compute=False and path=None raises NotImplementedError mentioning memoryview
When compute=False and writing to a file, store.sync() is called to ensure proper finalization
Store creation is delegated to get_writable_netcdf_store with group handling via get_child_store

task_7.title: Unify default netCDF write engine selection across Dataset and DataTree
task_7.description: The default backend engine for Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_netcdf() is now chosen consistently with open_dataset() and open_datatree(), dynamically selecting from available netCDF libraries with a preference order of netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy. Previously, DataTree.to_netcdf() hardcoded h5netcdf as the default engine, which caused a ModuleNotFoundError when only netCDF4 was installed. Additionally, Dataset.to_netcdf() defaulted to scipy when writing to file-like objects, regardless of other available libraries. Both paths now use the same unified engine resolution logic that respects the netCDF format being written and the target type.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree.to_netcdf() and Dataset.to_netcdf() dynamically select the default write engine based on installed netCDF libraries, rather than hardcoding a specific backend. Ensure that DataTree.to_netcdf() works when only netCDF4 is installed and h5netcdf is not. Ensure that the engine preference order (netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy) is consistent across all netCDF write paths and matches the read-side engine selection logic. Ensure that format-incompatible backends are excluded from candidates (e.g., scipy excluded for NETCDF4 format, h5netcdf excluded for NETCDF3 formats). Ensure that netcdf4 is excluded from candidates when writing to file-like objects or memoryview targets.

expectation.grounded: When engine=None, get_default_netcdf_write_engine() should be called to resolve the engine using NETCDF_BACKENDS_ORDER (netcdf4, h5netcdf, scipy). For DataTree.to_netcdf(), the engine resolution should pass format='NETCDF4' since groups require NETCDF4 format, which excludes scipy from candidates. For Dataset.to_netcdf() writing to a file-like object or memoryview, netcdf4 should be excluded from candidates. If the format starts with 'NETCDF3', h5netcdf should be excluded; if it starts with 'NETCDF4', scipy should be excluded. The first candidate whose module is importable should be returned. If no suitable backend is found, a ValueError should be raised with a message indicating the format and the list of suitable libraries that are not installed. The get_writable_netcdf_store() function should handle store creation with appropriate keyword arguments (autoclose, invalid_netcdf, auto_complex) and group handling should be done via store.get_child_store().
expectation.conceptual: When no engine is explicitly specified, both Dataset.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_netcdf() should automatically detect which netCDF backend libraries are installed and select the most preferred one that is compatible with the requested format and output target. The preference order should be netcdf4 first, then h5netcdf, then scipy. The selection should account for format constraints (some formats are not supported by all backends) and target type constraints (some backends cannot write to in-memory targets). If no compatible backend is available, a clear error should indicate which libraries could be installed to enable the operation.

constraints.grounded: The engine preference order netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy defined in NETCDF_BACKENDS_ORDER must be preserved. DataTree.to_netcdf() must not default to h5netcdf when engine is None. Dataset.to_netcdf() must not unconditionally default to scipy for file-like objects when engine is None. The engine selection for writing must be consistent with the engine selection for reading via open_dataset() and open_datatree(). Passing engine explicitly must still override the automatic selection. The invalid_netcdf option must only be accepted by the h5netcdf engine, raising ValueError for other engines.
constraints.conceptual: The automatic engine selection must never hardcode a single backend as the default. The write-side engine resolution must follow the same preference order as the read-side resolution. Explicitly specifying an engine must always take precedence over automatic selection. Existing code that passes engine explicitly must continue to work unchanged. The error messages when no suitable backend is found must be informative about which libraries are needed.

Dataset.to_netcdf() with engine=None writing to a file path now uses the unified engine selection (netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy) instead of a separate _get_default_engine() code path
Dataset.to_netcdf() with engine=None writing to a file-like object or memoryview now uses the unified engine selection with netcdf4 excluded, instead of unconditionally defaulting to scipy

task_9.title: Fix contour plot color normalization with logarithmic norms
task_9.description: Contour and contourf plots did not correctly normalize colors when using non-linear norms such as LogNorm or when passing a LogLocator. Xarray hardcoded a default of 7 linearly-spaced contour levels, overriding matplotlib's ability to choose levels appropriate for the active norm. Additionally, the colors parameter was only recognized when passed as a single string, causing list-form colors to be silently ignored in favor of the colormap. Both issues resulted in contour plots that used only a fraction of the colormap under logarithmic normalization, forcing users to manually specify log-spaced levels.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that contour and contourf plots correctly distribute colors across the full colormap when a non-linear norm (e.g., LogNorm) or a non-default locator (e.g., LogLocator) is provided. Ensure that the colors parameter is respected regardless of whether it is a single string or a sequence of color values.

expectation.grounded: When DataArray.plot.contourf or DataArray.plot.contour is called with a logarithmic norm (e.g., matplotlib.colors.LogNorm) and levels is not explicitly set, the function should defer level computation to matplotlib rather than forcing a fixed number of linearly-spaced levels. The _process_cmap_cbar_kwargs helper must not override levels to a hardcoded default when the caller has not specified levels. In the contour rendering path, when colors is any non-None value (string or sequence), cmap should be set to None and the colors value should be forwarded to matplotlib so it takes precedence over the colormap.
expectation.conceptual: Contour plots should automatically produce appropriately-spaced levels that match the given normalization scheme. When logarithmic normalization is active, the resulting plot should use the full range of the colormap with logarithmically distributed contour levels. When a user provides explicit colors (in any supported form), those colors should always be used instead of the colormap.

constraints.grounded: Contour and contourf plots with the default linear norm and no explicit levels must continue to produce the same visual output as before (matplotlib's own default level selection). Passing explicit levels must still override any automatic level computation. The colors parameter must remain mutually exclusive with cmap when colors is provided. Existing pcolormesh behavior must not be affected.
constraints.conceptual: Default linear-norm contour plots must not regress in appearance. Explicit user-provided levels must always take precedence. The fix must not alter behavior of non-contour plot types such as pcolormesh.

behavior: When levels is not explicitly provided in a contour or contourf call, xarray no longer forces a hardcoded default of 7 levels but instead defers to matplotlib's level auto-selection, which respects the active norm.
Under LogNorm or similar non-linear norms, contourf and contour now produce logarithmically-spaced levels by default, utilizing the full colormap range.
When the colors parameter is a non-None value of any type (string or sequence), it now takes precedence over cmap, which is set to None to avoid conflicts.
Previously, passing colors as a list to contour/contourf would silently fall through and use the cmap instead; this is now corrected.
acceptance_criteria: When calling DataArray.plot.contourf with norm=LogNorm(vmin, vmax) and no explicit levels, the resulting plot should display contour levels that are logarithmically spaced and use the full extent of the specified colormap.

When calling DataArray.plot.contourf with locator=ticker.LogLocator() and no explicit levels, the plot should respect the log locator and produce a properly log-scaled colorbar.
When calling DataArray.plot.contourf with colors specified as a list of color strings, the plot should use those colors instead of the colormap.
When calling DataArray.plot.contourf with colors specified as a single color string, the plot should continue to use that color (existing behavior preserved).

When calling DataArray.plot.contourf with explicit levels (e.g., levels=30), those explicit levels must be used regardless of the norm.

task_10.title: Fix auto_complex keyword argument forwarding for open_datatree
task_10.description: The auto_complex keyword argument was not properly forwarded through the DataTree I/O pipeline. When writing complex-valued data via DataTree.to_netcdf with auto_complex=True and reading it back with xr.open_datatree with auto_complex=True, the data was returned in its encoded structured dtype form (with 'r' and 'i' fields) instead of being automatically decoded back into native complex numbers. The fix ensures the auto_complex parameter is explicitly accepted and propagated through the DataTree netCDF read and write paths and the NetCDF4 backend entrypoint.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the auto_complex keyword argument is correctly distributed through the DataTree I/O code paths so that complex-valued data written via DataTree.to_netcdf(auto_complex=True) is properly decoded back into complex dtypes when read via xr.open_datatree(auto_complex=True) using the netcdf4 engine.

expectation.grounded: When xr.open_datatree is called with auto_complex=True and engine='netcdf4', the auto_complex parameter must be forwarded to the NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.open_datatree method and further into the underlying NetCDF4 store. Similarly, when DataTree.to_netcdf is called with auto_complex=True, the _datatree_to_netcdf implementation must accept and forward the auto_complex parameter explicitly rather than relying on **kwargs. The resulting DataTree variables should have native complex dtypes (e.g., complex128) rather than structured dtypes with 'r' and 'i' fields.
expectation.conceptual: When a user round-trips complex-valued data through DataTree netCDF serialization with auto_complex enabled on both write and read, the data should be transparently decoded back to complex number arrays. The read-side API should honor the auto_complex flag identically to how open_dataset already does.

constraints.grounded: The existing auto_complex behavior for xr.open_dataset and Dataset.to_netcdf must remain unaffected. The _datatree_to_netcdf function must explicitly declare auto_complex as a typed parameter (bool | None) rather than absorbing it via **kwargs. The NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint must pass auto_complex through in both its open_dataset and open_datatree methods.
constraints.conceptual: Fixing the DataTree path must not regress the existing Dataset-level complex number encoding/decoding. The parameter forwarding must be consistent across all DataTree I/O entry points that support the auto_complex option.

behavior: Previously, passing auto_complex=True to xr.open_datatree had no effect because the parameter was not forwarded to the backend store; data was returned with a structured dtype containing 'r' and 'i' fields instead of a complex dtype.

After the fix, auto_complex=True passed to xr.open_datatree is forwarded through NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint.open_datatree to the underlying store, causing complex-encoded data to be automatically decoded into native complex arrays.
The _datatree_to_netcdf function now accepts auto_complex as an explicit keyword parameter instead of relying on **kwargs, ensuring proper forwarding during write operations.
The NetCDF4BackendEntrypoint now passes auto_complex to the store constructor in both the open_dataset and open_datatree code paths.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataTree containing complex128 data is written to netCDF with auto_complex=True and read back via xr.open_datatree with auto_complex=True and engine='netcdf4', the resulting variable dtype should be complex128, not a structured dtype.
When xr.open_datatree is called with auto_complex=True, the parameter should be received and forwarded by the NetCDF4 backend entrypoint to the underlying store.
When DataTree.to_netcdf is called with auto_complex=True, the parameter should be accepted as an explicit keyword argument and forwarded through the write pipeline.
Existing auto_complex behavior for xr.open_dataset and Dataset.to_netcdf must continue to work unchanged.

Given a round-trip of complex-valued DataTree data through netCDF4 with auto_complex=True on both write and read, when inspecting the loaded DataTree's variable dtypes, they should match the original complex dtypes exactly.

task_11.title: Downgrade unlimited_dims encoding mismatch from error to warning
task_11.description: In version 2025.8.0, a strict validation was introduced in the _sanitize_unlimited_dims function that raises a ValueError when unlimited_dims references dimensions not present in the current dataset. This broke existing workflows where dataset.encoding['unlimited_dims'] carries over stale dimension names after subsetting operations (e.g., isel that drops a dimension). The fix differentiates between unlimited_dims originating from the explicit keyword argument (which still raises ValueError) and unlimited_dims inherited from dataset.encoding (which now emits a warning instead). This restores backward compatibility for common patterns like writing a subset of a dataset to netCDF while preserving strict validation for explicit API usage.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling to_netcdf on a dataset whose encoding['unlimited_dims'] references dimensions no longer present in the dataset (e.g., after subsetting with isel) does not raise a ValueError. The stale unlimited_dims inherited from dataset.encoding should produce a warning instead of an error, so that existing workflows that subset and re-save datasets are not broken.

expectation.grounded: When _sanitize_unlimited_dims detects undeclared dimensions in unlimited_dims, it must distinguish between two origins: (1) if the origin is the explicit unlimited_dims keyword argument, raise ValueError as before; (2) if the origin is dataset.encoding, call emit_user_level_warning with the same diagnostic message instead of raising. The function should still return the unlimited_dims value in both cases (non-raising path continues execution).
expectation.conceptual: When a dataset carries stale unlimited dimension names in its encoding metadata (e.g., after a dimension-reducing selection), writing that dataset to a file should succeed with a warning rather than failing with an error. Explicitly passing invalid unlimited_dims as a keyword argument should still raise an error to catch intentional misuse.

constraints.grounded: The ValueError must still be raised when unlimited_dims mismatch originates from the unlimited_dims keyword argument passed directly to to_netcdf. Only the dataset.encoding origin path should be downgraded to a warning via emit_user_level_warning. The warning message content should remain the same diagnostic text describing the undeclared dimensions.
constraints.conceptual: Strict validation must be preserved for explicit API calls where the user directly specifies unlimited_dims. Only inherited encoding metadata should receive lenient treatment. The user must still be informed of the mismatch through a visible warning so they can correct the encoding if desired.

behavior: When to_netcdf is called on a dataset whose encoding['unlimited_dims'] lists dimensions not present in the dataset's current dimensions, a user-level warning is emitted instead of raising ValueError.
When to_netcdf is called with an explicit unlimited_dims keyword argument containing dimensions not in the dataset, a ValueError is raised as before.
The warning message describes which unlimited dimensions are undeclared and suggests removing them from dataset.encoding.
The to_netcdf call completes successfully (file is written) when the mismatch originates from dataset.encoding, despite the stale unlimited_dims.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset with encoding['unlimited_dims'] referencing a dropped dimension (e.g., after isel) is written via to_netcdf, it should succeed and emit a warning instead of raising ValueError.
When to_netcdf is called with an explicit unlimited_dims keyword argument referencing a dimension not in the dataset, it should raise ValueError.
The emitted warning message should indicate which unlimited dimensions are not part of the current dataset dimensions and suggest removing them from dataset.encoding.

Given a dataset created with an unlimited dimension, when that dimension is removed via isel and the resulting subset is written to netCDF without explicitly passing unlimited_dims, then the write should complete without error.
Given a dataset where unlimited_dims is explicitly passed as a keyword argument to to_netcdf with a non-existent dimension, then a ValueError should be raised.

task_14.title: Fix auto_complex handling for open_datatree in NetCDF4 backend
task_14.description: The auto_complex feature, which handles automatic complex number type reconstruction from NetCDF4 data, did not function correctly when data was opened via open_datatree. This fix ensures that the auto_complex code path is properly invoked when using open_datatree, bringing parity with the behavior already working in open_dataset. Regression tests were added by running the existing TestNetCDF4Data suite through open_datatree as TestNetCDF4DataTree.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that complex number variables stored in NetCDF4 files are correctly reconstructed when opened via open_datatree. Previously, the auto_complex mechanism was not triggered on the open_datatree code path, causing complex-typed data to be returned in its raw split-component representation instead of as proper complex arrays.

expectation.grounded: When a NetCDF4 file containing complex-valued variables is opened via xarray.open_datatree with a NetCDF4-compatible backend, the auto_complex logic must activate and reconstruct complex dtypes in the resulting DataTree nodes, consistent with the behavior of open_dataset. The returned DataTree variables should have complex numpy dtypes (e.g., complex64, complex128) rather than separate real/imaginary component variables.
expectation.conceptual: Opening hierarchical NetCDF4 data containing complex numbers via the datatree API should automatically reconstruct complex-typed arrays, matching the behavior users already observe when opening the same data through the flat dataset API.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter the behavior of open_dataset or any other existing entry point. The NetCDF4 backend's handling of auto_complex for open_dataset must remain unchanged. The TestNetCDF4Data test suite, when run through open_datatree as TestNetCDF4DataTree, must pass without regressions.
constraints.conceptual: Existing dataset-level workflows and other backends must not be affected. The fix should only extend the already-working complex number reconstruction to the datatree code path without introducing side effects.

behavior: open_datatree now invokes the auto_complex reconstruction logic for NetCDF4 data, which was previously only active in the open_dataset path.
Complex-valued variables in NetCDF4 files are returned with proper complex dtypes when accessed through DataTree nodes.
The TestNetCDF4Data test suite is now additionally exercised through open_datatree as TestNetCDF4DataTree to guard against regressions on this code path.
acceptance_criteria: When a NetCDF4 file with complex-valued variables is opened via open_datatree, the resulting DataTree should contain variables with complex numpy dtypes (e.g., complex128) rather than raw split-component representations.
When the same NetCDF4 file is opened via open_dataset and via open_datatree, the complex-valued variable data should be equivalent in dtype and values.
When running the TestNetCDF4Data test suite through open_datatree (as TestNetCDF4DataTree), all tests should pass without modification.
When a NetCDF4 file without complex variables is opened via open_datatree, behavior should remain unchanged from the prior version.

task_13.title: Fix DataTree.to_netcdf hardcoded h5netcdf default engine and refactor store writing
task_13.description: DataTree.to_netcdf() had h5netcdf hardcoded as the default engine since 2025.8.0, causing a ModuleNotFoundError when only netcdf4 was installed. The fix replaces the hardcoded default with dynamic engine resolution based on installed dependencies and the requested format, aligning DataTree.to_netcdf() with the behavior of Dataset.to_netcdf(). Additionally, the internal writing path was refactored to use a single root store with child stores per subtree node, and compute=False is now supported when writing to file paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree.to_netcdf() does not hardcode h5netcdf as the default engine. When engine is not specified, the default engine must be resolved dynamically based on available backend libraries (preferring netcdf4, then h5netcdf, then scipy) and the requested format, consistent with Dataset.to_netcdf(). Ensure that calling DataTree.to_netcdf() without specifying engine succeeds when only netcdf4 is installed. Ensure that compute=False is supported for DataTree.to_netcdf() when writing to a file path.

expectation.grounded: When engine=None in DataTree.to_netcdf(), the function must call get_default_netcdf_write_engine() with format='NETCDF4' and the appropriate to_fileobject_or_memoryview flag to dynamically select the write engine. The candidate order is determined by NETCDF_BACKENDS_ORDER, filtered by format compatibility (NETCDF4 excludes scipy, NETCDF3 excludes h5netcdf) and target type (file-objects exclude netcdf4). If no suitable library is installed, a ValueError must be raised with a message naming the format and the candidate libraries. When compute=False and a file path is provided, DataTree.to_netcdf() must return a delayed write object via delayed_close_after_writes(). When compute=False and filepath is None (memoryview return), a NotImplementedError must be raised.
expectation.conceptual: When no engine is explicitly specified, DataTree.to_netcdf() should automatically select the best available netCDF backend library based on what is installed, with a preference for netcdf4 for disk-based writes. This behavior should be consistent with how Dataset.to_netcdf() resolves its default engine. If no compatible library is available, a clear error should be raised. Lazy (deferred) writing via compute=False should be supported when writing to a file path.

constraints.grounded: The engine resolution logic must not hardcode any single engine as the default. The candidate list must come from the plugin-registered NETCDF_BACKENDS_ORDER. Format-based filtering must exclude h5netcdf for NETCDF3 formats and scipy for NETCDF4 formats. Writing to file-objects must exclude netcdf4 from candidates. The DataTree writing path must open a single root store and use get_child_store() for subtree nodes rather than calling Dataset.to_netcdf() per node. compute=False must not raise NotImplementedError when a file path is provided. BytesIOProxy must be used instead of raw BytesIO for in-memory targets.
constraints.conceptual: Default engine selection must be dynamic and based on the user's installed libraries, never hardcoded. The writing process must handle all subtree nodes through a single store connection rather than independently opening and appending to the file per node. Deferred computation must be supported for file-based writes. In-memory writes must still require immediate computation.

behavior: When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with engine=None and only netcdf4 is installed, the write succeeds using the netcdf4 engine instead of raising ModuleNotFoundError for h5netcdf.
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with engine=None and only h5netcdf is installed, the write succeeds using h5netcdf.
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with engine=None and neither netcdf4 nor h5netcdf is installed, a ValueError is raised listing the candidate libraries.
The engine resolution respects format constraints: NETCDF4 formats exclude scipy, NETCDF3 formats exclude h5netcdf.
When writing to a file-object or memoryview target, netcdf4 is excluded from engine candidates.
DataTree.to_netcdf() with compute=False and a file path returns a delayed write object instead of raising NotImplementedError.
DataTree.to_netcdf() with compute=False and filepath=None raises NotImplementedError indicating memoryview returns do not support deferred computation.
All subtree nodes are written through a single root store using child stores, rather than through repeated Dataset.to_netcdf() calls that independently open and append to the file.
The store is properly closed after compute=True writes and synced after compute=False setup.

When DataTree.to_netcdf('file.nc') is called in an environment with h5netcdf installed but netcdf4 not installed, the file is written successfully without error.
When DataTree.to_netcdf('file.nc') is called with no netCDF libraries installed, a ValueError is raised mentioning the required libraries.

task_12.title: Eliminate redundant Dask computations in DataTree serialization with cross-group dependencies
task_12.description: DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() previously serialized each subtree node independently, each with its own store and ArrayWriter. This caused Dask arrays shared across groups to be computed multiple times, leading to significant performance overhead (50%+ in benchmarks). The fix unifies serialization so all subtree nodes write through a single root store and a single ArrayWriter, allowing the Dask scheduler to optimize the computation graph globally and execute each operation only once. Additionally, the DataTree.to_zarr() signature is expanded to explicitly accept parameters previously hidden behind **kwargs, and the consolidated parameter default changes from True to None.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() do not perform redundant Dask computations when the DataTree contains cross-group dependencies. When variables in different groups share upstream Dask graph nodes, each upstream operation should be computed exactly once during serialization, matching the efficiency of saving equivalent data as a single Dataset. Ensure that DataTree.to_zarr() explicitly exposes all Zarr-related write parameters (synchronizer, chunk_store, consolidated, append_dim, region, safe_chunks, align_chunks, storage_options, zarr_version, zarr_format, write_empty_chunks, chunkmanager_store_kwargs) rather than accepting them through **kwargs.

expectation.grounded: DataTree.to_netcdf() and DataTree.to_zarr() must use a single ArrayWriter across all subtree nodes and a single root store with get_child_store() for child groups, ensuring all Dask arrays are synced in one unified computation graph. The consolidated parameter on DataTree.to_zarr() should default to None instead of True. DataTree.to_zarr() should use subtree_with_keys for iteration and construct child stores using relative paths. When compute=False, both methods must return a dask.Delayed object produced via delayed_close_after_writes(). DataTree.to_netcdf() with compute=False when no file path is given must raise NotImplementedError. The AbstractDataStore must define a get_child_store() method, and NetCDF4DataStore, H5NetCDFStore, and ZarrStore must implement it. AbstractWritableDataStore must define a sync() method. Standalone factory functions get_writable_netcdf_store() and get_writable_zarr_store() must be available for creating writable stores.
expectation.conceptual: When a DataTree with cross-group Dask dependencies is saved to netCDF or Zarr, the serialization process should optimize the Dask computation graph globally across all groups. Each Dask task in the graph should execute only once regardless of how many groups reference it. The number of Dask task evaluations when saving a DataTree should match the number when saving the equivalent data as a single Dataset. All Zarr write options should be directly accessible as named parameters on DataTree.to_zarr(). When delayed computation is requested, a proper Dask delayed object should be returned that handles store finalization after writes complete.

constraints.grounded: Existing Dataset.to_netcdf() and Dataset.to_zarr() behavior must be preserved. The get_child_store() implementations on NetCDF4DataStore and H5NetCDFStore must compose group paths correctly when a parent group already exists. ZarrStore.get_child_store() must propagate all store configuration (mode, consolidate_on_close, append_dim, write_region, safe_chunks, write_empty, close_store_on_close, use_zarr_fill_value_as_mask, align_chunks, cache_members). Store close must happen in a finally block when compute=True, and sync must be called when compute=False. The consolidated metadata consolidation for Zarr must be handled via the store's consolidate_on_close mechanism rather than a separate explicit call. ZarrStore child stores must use relative paths for group names to avoid issues with consolidated metadata.
constraints.conceptual: Existing single-Dataset serialization workflows must not be affected. Child store creation must faithfully inherit all configuration from the parent store. Store lifecycle management (close and sync) must be robust against exceptions during writing. Zarr metadata consolidation must remain automatic and correct for DataTree writes. Child group paths must be constructed in a way that is compatible with the underlying storage backend's metadata handling.

behavior: DataTree.to_netcdf() opens a single root store and creates child stores via get_child_store() for each subtree node, rather than calling Dataset.to_netcdf() independently per node
DataTree.to_zarr() opens a single root ZarrStore and creates child stores via get_child_store() for each subtree node, rather than calling Dataset.to_zarr() independently per node
A single ArrayWriter is shared across all subtree nodes during DataTree serialization, causing all Dask arrays to be synced together in one computation
Cross-group Dask dependencies are computed exactly once instead of being redundantly re-evaluated per group
DataTree.to_zarr() consolidated parameter defaults to None instead of True

DataTree.to_zarr() accepts explicit keyword parameters (synchronizer, chunk_store, consolidated, append_dim, region, safe_chunks, align_chunks, storage_options, zarr_version, zarr_format, write_empty_chunks, chunkmanager_store_kwargs) instead of **kwargs
DataTree.to_netcdf() with compute=False and no file path raises NotImplementedError
When compute=False, both serialization methods return a dask.Delayed that finalizes the store after writes complete
When compute=True, the store is closed in a finally block ensuring cleanup on errors
When compute=False, the store is synced (not closed) after setting up writes
ZarrStore.get_child_store() uses require_group() to create or access child Zarr groups and inherits all parent configuration
NetCDF4DataStore.get_child_store() and H5NetCDFStore.get_child_store() compose group paths and share the same file manager
Zarr metadata consolidation is handled by the root store's consolidate_on_close mechanism rather than a separate consolidate_metadata() call
acceptance_criteria: When a DataTree has Dask arrays with cross-group dependencies and is saved via to_zarr(), each Dask task should execute exactly once, matching the evaluation count of saving equivalent data as a single Dataset

When a DataTree has Dask arrays with cross-group dependencies and is saved via to_netcdf(), each Dask task should execute exactly once, matching the evaluation count of saving equivalent data as a single Dataset
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with compute=True, the resulting Zarr store should contain all groups and variables with correct data
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with compute=False, it should return a dask.Delayed object that, when computed, writes all data and closes the store
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with compute=True, the resulting netCDF file should contain all groups and variables with correct data
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with compute=False and a file path, it should return a dask.Delayed object that, when computed, writes all data and closes the store
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with compute=False and no file path, it should raise NotImplementedError
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with consolidated=None (the new default), metadata should be consolidated on close for new writes
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called with explicit parameters like synchronizer, chunk_store, storage_options, safe_chunks, or align_chunks, these should be correctly passed to the underlying ZarrStore
When an error occurs during dump_to_store within DataTree serialization, the store should still be properly closed (compute=True) or synced (compute=False)
When DataTree.to_netcdf() is called with write_inherited_coords=True, inherited coordinates should be written to child groups correctly
When DataTree.to_zarr() is called, Zarr child groups should use relative paths to avoid issues with consolidated metadata
